saints.name: St. Botulph
saints.title: Abbot
saints.shortBlurb: An English abbot whose name lives on in the town of Boston, “Botolph's town”…
biography: Born of noble Saxon parents in the early seventh century, Botulph, or Botolph, was educated with his brother Adulph under Fursey at Cnobheresburg and became a Benedictine on the Continent. Returning to England, he found favour with a king of the southern Angles, who granted him a tract of desolate land on which to build a monastery.

The Anglo-Saxon Chronicle records under the year 654 that 'Botolph began to build the church at Ikanho.' His monastery of Icanho — 'ox hill,' identified with Iken in Suffolk — drew many disciples, and the biographer of Ceolfrith, writing in Bede's day, remembers him as a man of remarkable life and learning. He died about 680 and was buried at his own foundation.

In 970 his relics were moved inland for fear of the Danes, and in time they rested at Thorney Abbey. More than sixty ancient English churches bear his name, four of them at the gates of London, where travelers prayed for a safe journey — whence he is the patron of travelers. Boston, 'Botolph's town,' keeps his name in two hemispheres.
saints.knownFor: Founding the abbey of Icanho; patron of travelers.
